content.value_statement: Azure hosted agents require correct SDK objects, container settings, and identity configuration. This skill gives Python patterns for creating, listing, and deleting hosted agent versions.
actual_capabilities: Shows the required Azure AI Projects SDK version and project endpoint variable.
Configures AIProjectClient with DefaultAzureCredential for Python workflows.
Creates ImageBasedHostedAgentDefinition settings for protocol, image, CPU, memory, tools, and environment variables.
Lists and deletes hosted agent versions with Azure AI Projects SDK calls.
Provides a Python async pattern for hosted agent creation.
Explains common hosted agent errors and practical fixes.
limitations: Does not build or publish container images.
Does not create Azure resources, identities, or ACR role assignments.
Requires validation against current Azure service availability and SDK behavior.
Uses placeholder images, endpoints, and MCP server URLs.

use_cases.title: Prototype Hosted Agents
use_cases.description: Create a first Azure AI Foundry hosted agent from a custom container image.

use_cases.title: Prepare Deployment Settings
use_cases.description: Review required image paths, resource sizing, environment variables, and ACR permissions before deployment.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Agent Versions
use_cases.description: Map common hosted agent errors to likely causes and corrective actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a basic Azure AI Foundry hosted agent in Python using my container image and project endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Resources and Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the CPU, memory, tools, and environment variables for a Python hosted agent that uses code interpreter and file search.

prompt_templates.title: Add MCP Tooling
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to configure an Azure hosted agent with code interpreter and an MCP server, using safe placeholder values.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my hosted agent deployment plan for image versioning, ACR permissions, resource sizing, secrets handling, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: I need a first hosted agent from an ACR image.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines the endpoint variable, credential setup, hosted agent definition, image setting, protocol choice, and version creation step.

output_examples.input: My hosted agent cannot pull its image.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies ACR pull permissions as the likely issue and recommends checking the project managed identity role assignment.

output_examples.input: I want a production review before rollout.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks image tags, resource settings, environment variables, tool choices, error handling, and cleanup expectations.

best_practices: Use specific container image tags for production releases.
Store secrets outside the skill examples, such as in Azure Key Vault.
Verify ACR pull permissions before creating a hosted agent version.
anti_patterns: Using the latest image tag for production agent versions.
Hardcoding secrets in hosted agent environment variables.
Connecting MCP endpoints without reviewing the remote server and data access.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Azure AI Foundry hosted agents from container images using Python SDK examples.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users must create resources and permissions in their Azure environment.

faq.question: Which SDK version is covered?
faq.answer: The skill references azure-ai-projects version 2.0.0b3 or later for hosted agent support.

faq.question: Can it help with ACR image pull errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common image pull failures and points users to managed identity AcrPull permissions.

faq.question: Does it include async Python guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an async hosted agent creation pattern using Azure identity and projects clients.

faq.question: Is this a substitute for Azure documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a focused implementation guide and should be validated against current Azure documentation.
